background: The Co-operative Bank is a UK retail and small-business bank, funded by retail deposits and lending mainly on residential mortgages, which became a subsidiary of Coventry Building Society after its rescue and years of restructuring.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the bank, A- on average, one on a positive outlook and one on a stable outlook, after a one-notch downgrade by one of the three on 16 Sep 2026 and a move to positive outlook by one on 23 Oct 2026. Capital is strong on a risk-weighted basis, with CET1 of 19.3% in the top quarter of UK mid-sized banks, but leverage of 4.6% is in the bottom quarter, the figure to watch. Liquidity sits around the middle of the peer group, with LCR of 174% above the median and NSFR of 139% just below it. Since 31 Dec 2024 CET1 and leverage have each risen 0.6 points while LCR has fallen 19 points.
